name: Sentio: AI Pages and Widgets for Elementor
author: Sentio Addons

sections.description:
Sentio AI builds an Elementor page for you. Tell it what the page is for, hand it a mockup, or paste the address of a site you like. It plans the page, writes it, lays it out with native Elementor containers and widgets, and adds the motion.

What you get is an ordinary Elementor page. You can edit every part of it by hand, and it keeps working if you switch Sentio AI off.

It starts free: 36 credits, about three pages. No card, and no AI account or API key of your own.

Documentation | Plans | Credit terms

Five ways to start

  • From your words. Say what the page is for. Sentio asks a question or two, shows you what it will build and what it costs, then builds it.
  • From your mockup. Attach a picture or a PDF of a design. Sentio builds it as designed.
  • From a site you like. Paste its address. Sentio builds your own version of its layout and motion, ready for your content.
  • A cinematic page. Attach your own film. Sentio builds the page around it, and the film plays as visitors scroll.
  • A ready-made page. Ten finished cinematic pages, most with a film. Pick one and it is on your site as a draft in seconds, with its film and pictures, for no credits. Each card keeps the prompt that made it, so you can copy it and make your own.

After the build

Ask for a change in plain words, or use the one-click options: Apply my brand, Bolder, Calmer. Undo works as it always does in Elementor. Save and Publish stay yours: Sentio never publishes anything.

Sentio Studio pictures

When a page needs pictures you don’t have, Sentio Studio makes them for that page, in its style. Sentio asks first. Each picture costs 2 credits and is saved to your Media Library.

Credits

  • 36 free credits come with the plugin, once per site. They never expire.
  • A page costs 12 credits. A Sentio Studio picture costs 2. A change you ask Sentio to make costs 1.
  • Free: ready-made pages, Apply my brand, Bolder, Calmer, and everything you edit by hand.
  • You see the cost before every build, and a build never takes more than it said.
  • A build cut short before the whole page arrives gives its credits back.
  • Want more? Sentio Premium is a separate plugin with credits every month (200, 420 or 990), enough for films made for your page. The credit terms say how credits refill and how long they last.

What Sentio AI never does

It is off until an administrator switches it on, and nothing is sent anywhere before that. It runs only in the WordPress admin and the Elementor editor, for someone signed in. It never runs on your published pages, never writes PHP or files of code to your site, never installs anything, and never publishes. Every widget works the same with it off.

65 widgets

Sentio is also a widget library. 65 widgets come with this plugin. Each has full content and style controls, loads only its own CSS and JavaScript on the pages that use it, and is built for keyboard and screen-reader use.

  • Content and layout: Accordion, Advanced Alert, Animated Headline, Animated Timeline, Bento Grid, Blockquote, Button, Fancy Divider, Flip Box, Info Box, Nested Accordion, Nested Carousel, Nested Tabs, Off-Canvas, Progress Tracker, Shortcode, Skeleton Loader, Tabs, Tooltip.
  • Motion and media: 3D Product Viewer, Audio Player, Image Gallery, Ken Burns Hero Slider, Logo Carousel, Lottie, Media Playlist, Pinned Story, Scroll Film, Scroll Glow, Scroll Showcase, Slideshow, Split Text, Video Carousel.
  • Marketing: Call to Action, Count Up, Countdown, Counter Cards, Mortgage Calculator, Price List, Price Table, Property Card, Reviews, Skills Measurement, Social Share, Team Members, Testimonial Carousel.
  • Posts and site: Archive Posts, Author Info Card, Featured Image, Page Title, Portfolio, Post Comments, Post Excerpt, Post Info, Post Navigation, Posts, Site Logo, Site Title, Sitemap, Yoast Breadcrumbs.
  • Navigation and tools: Google Maps, Nav Menu, Scroll to Top, Search, Single Page Navigation.

Sentio Premium

Sentio Premium is a separate plugin from sentioaddons.com. It adds credits every month, films made for your pages by Sentio Studio, advanced motion (pins, scrubs, smooth scrolling) and 171 widgets in all, with sets for WooCommerce, The Events Calendar and ACF. Premium’s extra widgets show in the Elementor panel as locked entries. They are names only: no Premium code ships in this plugin.

External services

Sentio AI is off until an administrator switches it on, and nothing below that belongs to it is contacted before then. The other services are contacted only by a widget you place, or after you opt in. Nothing about your visitors is ever sent to Sentio.

sentioaddons.com: your Sentio AI account and credits

Needed to switch Sentio AI on and to count credits. Requests are made by your server.

  • When you switch it on: your site’s address, this plugin’s name and version, the email address you enter, and whether you ticked the updates box go to https://sentioaddons.com/wp-json/sentio-lm/v1/ai/register. Sentio emails that address a 6-digit code; the code you type is checked at /ai/verify-code.
  • When you open the Sentio AI panel or the Sentio dashboard: your site’s address and its registration token, to read your credit balance (/ai/status, /ai/credits/balance).
  • Before and after each build or change: the same, with what kind of thing is being made (a page, a picture, a change), and afterwards whether it worked and how much AI it used (/ai/authorize, /ai/report, /ai/credits/quote, /ai/credits/free, /ai/credits/result). Your words and your page’s content are never sent here.
  • To give free credits once per site, the service calls your site back once at /wp-json/sentio/v1/ai/credit-challenge. Your site answers with a proof that it holds the registration, and nothing else.

Sentio uses Klaviyo (Klaviyo, Inc.) to store the email address behind a free account, and to send you Sentio updates only if you ticked that box. This plugin never talks to Klaviyo itself.

  • Terms: https://sentioaddons.com/credit-terms/
  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai
  • Klaviyo privacy: https://www.klaviyo.com/legal/privacy/privacy-notice

Sentio’s AI service: building and changing pages

Needed to plan and write a page. It is run by Sentio (Sensus Media) on Google Cloud, at addresses the account service hands out (today https://generate-gsbgom2zpa-uc.a.run.app and https://engine-gsbgom2zpa-uc.a.run.app). It passes what a build needs to Anthropic, whose models do the writing. Some requests are made by your server and others by your browser while you work in the Elementor editor.

Sent when you build a page or ask for a change:

  • the words you type and your answers to Sentio’s questions;
  • what you attach: a mockup or PDF is sent whole; photos and a logo as small copies; stills from a film, never the film itself;
  • a web address you give it. The service opens that page to read its layout and motion;
  • the settings and text of the part of the page you are changing, and pictures of the page in the editor, so the result can be checked;
  • your Elementor global colours and fonts; your site’s title, tagline and language; your site brief, when you let Sentio use it; the title, alt text and address of recent images in your Media Library; and on a product page, that WooCommerce product’s public details.

Not sent: anything about your visitors, your other pages, or your site’s users and passwords.

  • Terms: https://sentioaddons.com/credit-terms/
  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai
  • Anthropic terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms
  • Anthropic privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

fal.ai: Sentio Studio pictures

Used only when you say yes to “Add pictures from Sentio Studio?”. Your browser sends Sentio’s AI service a short description written by your site (the page’s subject, colours and look) and, where there is one, the picture to start from. The service passes them to fal.ai, which makes the picture. Your server then downloads the finished file from fal.ai’s file host (*.fal.media) into your Media Library.

  • fal.ai terms: https://fal.ai/terms
  • fal.ai privacy: https://fal.ai/privacy

Pixabay: stock photos

When a page built from your words has places for photos and you have none, Sentio’s AI service searches Pixabay with a few words about the page. Your server then downloads the photos it uses from https://pixabay.com/ into your Media Library, each credited to its photographer. Pixabay receives the search words from Sentio, and an ordinary download request from your server.

  • Pixabay terms: https://pixabay.com/service/terms/
  • Pixabay privacy: https://pixabay.com/service/privacy/

sentioaddons.com: ready-made pages, their films and preview clips

Only after Sentio AI is switched on. When you pick a ready-made page, your server downloads that page, its pictures and its film from https://sentioaddons.com/wp-content/uploads/sentio-demo/ and checks every file before keeping it. The cards on Sentio → AI and the dashboard also play short preview clips from the same folder, loaded by your browser. These are ordinary downloads: they carry your site’s address, as every request from WordPress does, and nothing else.

  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai

A site you point Sentio at

When you ask Sentio to build from a web address, Sentio’s AI service visits that address. A page built this way uses that site’s own pictures and films as stand-ins, linked from where they are, until you replace them with yours: while they are on your page, your visitors’ browsers load them from that site. On Sentio → AI → Direction, “match a site” makes your server read the address you type, and its stylesheets, to pick up its colours and fonts.

Google Fonts

A page Sentio builds or places uses the fonts its design calls for. When those are Google fonts, your visitors’ browsers load them from https://fonts.googleapis.com and https://fonts.gstatic.com, as they do for any Elementor page that uses Google fonts. The Elementor editor loads them the same way while you work.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Google Maps

Widget: Google Maps. Your visitor’s browser loads https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js only when a Google Maps widget is on the page and you have set a Google API key. With no key the widget contacts nobody. Data sent: your API key and the standard Maps JavaScript API load parameters.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/maps/terms-20180207
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

YouTube

Widgets: Media Playlist, Video Carousel, Portfolio, only when you give one a YouTube address. Your visitor’s browser loads the thumbnail from https://img.youtube.com/, the player from https://www.youtube.com/embed/ and the playback API from https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api. Data sent: the public video ID.

  • Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Vimeo

Widgets: Media Playlist, Video Carousel, Portfolio, only when you give one a Vimeo address. Your visitor’s browser loads the player from https://player.vimeo.com/. When no thumbnail is set by hand, your server also asks https://vimeo.com/api/oembed.json for one. Data sent: the public video ID or address.

  • Terms: https://vimeo.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://vimeo.com/privacy

cdnjs (Cloudflare): the Lottie player

Widget: Lottie. A page with a Lottie widget loads the lottie-web player, version 5.12.2, from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/, and the animation file from the address you give the widget. Data sent: nothing beyond the request itself.

  • Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
  • Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

sentioaddons.com: usage data (opt-in)

Off unless you tick the unticked usage-data box on the welcome screen, or opt in at Sentio → Version. Then your server posts once a day to https://sentioaddons.com/wp-json/sentio-lm/v1/telemetry: this plugin’s name and version, your WordPress and PHP versions, your theme’s family, your site’s language, a one-way hash of your site’s address, and how many of each Sentio widget your pages use. Opting out at Sentio → Version asks the service to delete your site’s row (/telemetry/site) and stops the daily post.

  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/

sentioaddons.com: backlink (per widget, off by default)

Makes no request. A switch on each widget’s Advanced tab, off by default, adds a plain link to that widget’s page on sentioaddons.com. Listed here so nothing is left out.

License

Sentio: AI Pages and Widgets for Elementor is free software released under the GNU General Public License v2 (or later); see https://www.gnu.org/licenses/gpl-2.0.html.

Third-Party Libraries

This plugin bundles the following GPL-compatible libraries:

  • Lottie Web (MIT) — https://github.com/airbnb/lottie-web
  • Marker Clusterer (Apache 2.0) — https://github.com/googlemaps/js-markerclusterer
  • html-to-image (MIT) — https://github.com/bubkoo/html-to-image

It also bundles two fonts for the welcome screen, served from the plugin (no request to Google Fonts):

  • Poppins (SIL Open Font License 1.1) — https://github.com/itfoundry/Poppins
  • Cinzel (SIL Open Font License 1.1) — https://github.com/NDISCOVER/Cinzel

MIT, Apache 2.0 and the SIL Open Font License are GPL-compatible licenses. The font licences ship in assets/fonts/onboarding/.

The carousel widgets (Reviews, Testimonial, Logo, Slideshow, Video Carousel, Posts) consume the Swiper library via Elementor’s bundled swiper script handle; Swiper is not bundled by this plugin.
sections.installation:
1. In WordPress, go to Plugins → Add New, search for “Sentio: AI Pages and Widgets for Elementor”, then Install and Activate. Or upload the ZIP at Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Make sure Elementor (the free plugin, 3.20 or newer) is installed and active.
  3. The welcome screen opens. To use Sentio AI, enter your email and the 6-digit code it sends you. Or press Not now: every widget works without it.
  4. Go to Sentio → Dashboard and pick a way to start, or edit any page with Elementor and open the Sentio AI tab.
  5. Sentio’s widgets are in the Elementor panel under the Sentio categories.
sections.faq:
Is it really free?

Yes. The plugin, its 65 widgets and the ten ready-made pages are free. Sentio AI comes with 36 free credits, once per site, which is about three pages. There is no card and no trial clock.

What do credits buy?

A page costs 12 credits, a Sentio Studio picture 2, and a change you ask Sentio to make 1. Ready-made pages, the one-click options and your own edits are free. You see the cost before every build.

Do I need my own AI account or API key?

No. Sentio AI runs on Sentio’s own service. There is nothing to set up and no separate bill.

Do I need Elementor Pro?

No. Sentio works with the free Elementor plugin, version 3.20 or newer.

Can I edit what Sentio builds?

Yes, all of it. Pages are built from native Elementor containers and widgets, so every heading, picture, colour and section is an ordinary Elementor element.

What is a ready-made page?

A finished page Sentio built from one prompt, packaged with its film and pictures. Picking one places a copy on your site as a new draft, in seconds and for no credits. Its colours and fonts live on the page itself, so nothing is added to your site’s global styles.

What happens when my credits run out?

Nothing breaks. Your pages and widgets keep working, and you can still place ready-made pages and edit by hand. To build more with AI, Sentio Premium has plans with credits every month.

What if a build stops halfway?

If it was cut short before the whole page arrived, its credits come back by themselves. If the whole page had arrived, they stay used.

What does Sentio AI send, and where?

Only what a build needs, only when someone signed in uses it, and never anything about your visitors. The External services section below lists every service, what is sent and when.

Does Sentio AI run on my published pages?

No. It runs in the WordPress admin and the Elementor editor. Published pages are plain Elementor pages.

Does it collect usage data?

Only if you tick the box on the welcome screen. It is unticked by default, and you can opt out at Sentio → Version at any time.

What happens if I install Sentio Premium?

This plugin switches itself off while Premium is active, and Premium takes over the same widgets and pages. Nothing you built is lost.

How do I remove it cleanly?

Deactivate and delete it at Plugins → Installed Plugins. Pages you built stay as they are. For bugs, use the WordPress.org support forum or email support@sentioaddons.com.
sections.changelog:
3.0.0 — 2026-11-15

Sentio AI now builds whole pages, and the plugin is now called Sentio: AI Pages and Widgets for Elementor.

  • Feature: Build a page in Elementor from your words, from a mockup (a picture or a PDF), from a site you like, or around your own film. Sentio asks a question or two, shows what it will build and what it costs, and builds it from native Elementor containers and widgets, with motion. Nothing in Sentio AI is locked in this plugin.
  • Feature: Ten ready-made cinematic pages. Pick one on Sentio → Dashboard or Sentio → AI and it is placed as a new draft, with its film and pictures, in seconds and for no credits.
  • Feature: Sentio Studio pictures, made for the page being built, at 2 credits each.
  • Feature: Credits. Every site gets 36 free credits, about three pages. A page costs 12, a Studio picture 2, a change you ask for 1. The cost is shown before every build, and a build cut short before the whole page arrives gives its credits back.
  • Feature: Scroll Film, a film that plays as visitors scroll, is now a free widget.
  • Feature: A new welcome and a new dashboard: pick a way to start, see your credits and your pages.
  • Changed: Sentio AI runs on the Sentio service only. The option to connect your own Anthropic, OpenAI or Google account is gone.
  • Changed: The free allowance is counted in credits, not page builds.
  • See External services for what Sentio AI sends, to whom and when.

2.1.1 — 2026-09-09

  • Fix fatal error on update becuase upload directory corruption.

2.1.0 — 2026-09-02

New: Sentio AI, which sets a widget up for you from a plain-English description.

  • Feature: Sentio AI — a Sentio AI box inside every Sentio widget. Describe what you want in your own words, press Generate, and that widget’s settings are filled in for you: layout, content, colors and fonts taken from your Elementor palette, and an image chosen from your media library. Only the widget you are editing is touched, and Undo reverses it like any other edit.
  • Feature: Follow-up prompts refine the widget you already have rather than starting over, so you can change one thing at a time — “make the button coral and a bit wider” — instead of rewriting the whole description. Each widget suggests an example prompt to start from.
  • Feature: Two ways to run it, chosen at Sentio → Extensions. Use the Sentio AI service, which includes a monthly allowance of generations, or connect your own Anthropic, OpenAI or Google account and generate without a limit, billed to you by that provider.
  • Feature: Off until you turn it on. Nothing is sent anywhere — not even a registration — until an administrator enables it and accepts the notice shown in the editor, and you can disconnect at any time from the same screen. Every widget and every control works exactly as before with the AI off, unused, or out of allowance; nothing is locked or reduced. See External services above for what a generation sends.
  • Feature: New Extensions tab in the Sentio dashboard, where optional features such as Sentio AI are switched on and configured.

2.0.8 — 2026-08-21

Carousel independence, Ken Burns playback, and structured-data validity fixes.

  • Fix: Reviews Carousel, Testimonial Carousel and Video Carousel — when two or more carousels of the same type were placed on one page, the first carousel’s arrows and dots controlled all of them. Each carousel’s navigation now drives only its own slides.
  • Fix: Ken Burns Hero Slider — autoplay never started, so the slider stayed on the first slide until it was clicked. It now advances on its own at the configured speed.
  • Fix: Ken Burns Hero Slider — the slow zoom and pan eased to a near stop partway through each slide, and did not start again when a slide came back around. The movement now runs at a steady rate for the whole time a slide is on screen and restarts each time that slide returns. Its duration is derived from the autoplay and transition speeds, so it no longer finishes early and sits still.
  • Fix: Video Carousel — video structured data did not include an upload date, so Google reported the items as invalid for video rich results. A new optional “Upload Date” setting was added; leave it empty to use the post’s own publish date.
  • Fix: Structured data in Accordion, Property Card, Reviews Carousel, Testimonial Carousel and Video Carousel — partial structured data is no longer written to the page. If a property Google requires is missing, the whole block is left out rather than published in an incomplete form that search engines report as invalid. Reviews with no author name or no rating are skipped instead of being written out empty.

2.0.7 — 2026-07-31

New free widget: Skeleton Loader. Shortcode widget fix.

  • Feature: New Skeleton Loader widget (Advanced Components) — a skeleton loader / skeleton screen you can place on the canvas and point at a container or CSS selector, or use as a standalone placeholder. Skeleton shapes are inferred from the target’s own markup and measurements, so the placeholder matches the real content instead of being a generic grey box.
  • Feature: Skeleton Loader is also available from the Advanced tab of any Elementor element — including core Elementor widgets and third-party addon widgets — with per-element mode, target, timing and styling.
  • Feature: Global defaults at Sentio → Skeleton Loader — base and shimmer colors (optionally derived from your Elementor palette), animation style and speed, corner radius, minimum display time and failsafe timeout. Per-element settings override them.
  • Feature: Three loading behaviors. Additive for load-more and infinite scroll appends skeleton cards after your existing posts and never disturbs them. Replacement for pagination and filtering takes the outgoing posts out of flow and shows skeletons in their place. Deferred embed covers video, map and booking iframes until the embed itself is ready.
  • Fix: Shortcode widget — shortcode output is no longer filtered before display. It was previously passed through a content filter that removed <script>, <form>, <input>, <textarea>, <select> and <iframe> tags while keeping the script’s inner text, so a Gravity Forms shortcode rendered a form with no fields followed by its own JavaScript printed as visible text on the page. Form, embed and script shortcodes (Gravity Forms, Contact Form 7, WooCommerce and others) now render exactly as the originating plugin produced them.
  • Accessibility: skeletons are hidden from assistive technology, shimmer stops for visitors who prefer reduced motion, and nothing is ever hidden from visitors with JavaScript disabled.
  • Reliability: a failsafe timeout always clears the skeleton if the readiness signal never arrives, and a minimum display time prevents a sub-second flicker.

2.0.6 — 2026-07-23

New free widget: Mortgage Calculator.

  • Feature: New Mortgage Calculator widget (Advanced Components) — a live monthly-payment estimator with principal & interest plus optional property taxes, insurance, HOA fees, and auto-applied PMI when the down payment is under 20%. Includes a percent/amount down-payment toggle, loan-term presets with optional custom entry, a cost-breakdown donut chart, a collapsible year-by-year amortization table, an optional call-to-action button, and a configurable disclaimer. All calculations run locally in the browser and on your server — the widget contacts no external services.

2.0.5 — 2026-06-25

Ken Burns alignment, breadcrumb structured-data, and Elementor editor preview fixes.

  • Fix: Ken Burns hero — CTA buttons now follow the content Text Alignment control.
  • Fix: Breadcrumbs — item URL property now emits correctly (was stripped by an incorrect escaper).
  • Fix: Breadcrumbs — structured-data position now emits (was silently dropped).
  • Fix: Widget styles now preview correctly in the Elementor editor.

2.0.4 — 2026-06-16

Reliability fix so Sentio’s widget categories register correctly alongside other Elementor add-ons, plus first-run and dashboard refinements.

  • Fix: Sentio widget categories now register reliably when other Elementor add-on plugins that register their own categories early (for example event/calendar or all-in-one widget add-ons) are active. Sentio now subscribes to Elementor’s category-registration step earlier, so its panel categories no longer fail to appear.
  • Fix: The welcome screen now opens immediately on first activation, instead of only after navigating to a Sentio page later.
  • Fix: Third-party admin notices no longer display inside the Sentio dashboard or welcome header banner; they now appear in WordPress’s standard position above it. No notices are suppressed or hidden.
  • Feature: Added a dismissible “leave a review” invitation in the dashboard’s LITE comparison card.

2.0.3 — 2026-05-30

This release removes all admin notice suppression code per the WordPress.org plugin review.

  • Removed 231 lines of code that suppressed third-party admin notices on Sentio admin screens via remove_action() calls on admin_notices, in_admin_header, and related hooks. Standard WordPress notice behavior is now restored across all Sentio admin pages.
  • Removed CSS rules that hid third-party plugin notice elements (Freemius, Jetpack, Yoast, etc.) when they appeared inside Sentio admin layouts. Foreign notices now render normally at their natural injection points.
  • No replacement suppression mechanism added. Users will see standard WordPress admin notices from core, security plugins, and other addons as designed.

2.0.2 — 2026-05-20

This release addresses the inline

  • Refactored admin page CSS into a single registered stylesheet enqueued via wp_enqueue_style() on Sentio admin screens, replacing prior per-page conditional enqueueing that did not handle JavaScript-driven tab navigation correctly.
  • Extracted inline style attributes from the Locked Widget render output to a dedicated stylesheet (assets/css/widgets/locked-widget-notice.css), registered as a Sentio handle and auto-enqueued via Elementor’s get_style_depends() pattern. Render output now uses BEM-style class names instead of inline style attributes.
  • Improved CSS class name escaping by using sanitize_html_class() for class identifiers per WordPress canonical patterns.

2.0.1 — 2026-05-13

This release addresses all feedback from the WordPress.org plugin review.

  • Replaced 73 instances of output requiring escaping with canonical wp_kses(), tag_escape(), and esc_*() patterns. Escaping now happens at every output site, not at variable construction, per the “escape late” principle.
  • Added per-field sanitization for the AJAX POST settings handler in the Posts widget. Each of the ~40 settings fields now receives context-appropriate sanitization (absint, sanitize_key, tag_escape, in_array whitelist) at the JSON-decode boundary.
  • Refactored four direct database queries to use WordPress core APIs: comment counting now uses get_comments(), WooCommerce product enumeration uses wc_get_products(), and The Events Calendar venue/organizer lookups use get_posts().
  • Replaced one variable-based translation argument with static literal __() calls via a translation lookup table, so translation tooling can extract strings correctly.
  • Added nonce verification before processing form data in admin pages, including refactoring the admin page router to use get_current_screen() instead of $_GET parameters.
  • Prefixed file-global variables in admin templates with the sentio_ prefix per WordPress naming conventions.
  • Removed phpcs:ignore suppression comments throughout the plugin and addressed each underlying issue with real code changes rather than suppression.
  • Removed the debug_log() development helper from production code paths.

2.0.0

  • 53 free widgets organized across content, marketing, posts and dynamic content, navigation, media, and tools.
  • 99 additional PREMIUM widgets shown as locked stubs in the Elementor widget panel; clicking a locked widget opens an upsell card.
  • Per-widget CSS and JavaScript asset loading — assets are loaded only on pages where the widget is actually placed; no global frontend bundle.
  • WCAG 2.1 AA compliance across newly-authored widgets (keyboard navigation, ARIA landmarks, focus indicators, live-region announcements, prefers-reduced-motion respect). Pre-existing widgets are being retroactively audited.
  • Consent-gated daily telemetry phone-home — opt-in at activation, one-click opt-out at any time from Sentio → Version. See External services above for full data-field disclosure.
  • Updates delivered through the WordPress.org core updater.
  • Translation-ready: all UI strings localizable via the sentio-widgets-for-elementor text domain.

Ask for a change in plain words, or use the one-click options: Apply my brand, Bolder, Calmer. Undo works as it always does in Elementor. Save and Publish stay yours: Sentio never publishes anything.

Sentio Studio pictures

When a page needs pictures you don’t have, Sentio Studio makes them for that page, in its style. Sentio asks first. Each picture costs 2 credits and is saved to your Media Library.

Credits

  • 36 free credits come with the plugin, once per site. They never expire.
  • A page costs 12 credits. A Sentio Studio picture costs 2. A change you ask Sentio to make costs 1.
  • Free: ready-made pages, Apply my brand, Bolder, Calmer, and everything you edit by hand.
  • You see the cost before every build, and a build never takes more than it said.
  • A build cut short before the whole page arrives gives its credits back.
  • Want more? Sentio Premium is a separate plugin with credits every month (200, 420 or 990), enough for films made for your page. The credit terms say how credits refill and how long they last.

What Sentio AI never does

It is off until an administrator switches it on, and nothing is sent anywhere before that. It runs only in the WordPress admin and the Elementor editor, for someone signed in. It never runs on your published pages, never writes PHP or files of code to your site, never installs anything, and never publishes. Every widget works the same with it off.

65 widgets

Sentio is also a widget library. 65 widgets come with this plugin. Each has full content and style controls, loads only its own CSS and JavaScript on the pages that use it, and is built for keyboard and screen-reader use.

  • Content and layout: Accordion, Advanced Alert, Animated Headline, Animated Timeline, Bento Grid, Blockquote, Button, Fancy Divider, Flip Box, Info Box, Nested Accordion, Nested Carousel, Nested Tabs, Off-Canvas, Progress Tracker, Shortcode, Skeleton Loader, Tabs, Tooltip.
  • Motion and media: 3D Product Viewer, Audio Player, Image Gallery, Ken Burns Hero Slider, Logo Carousel, Lottie, Media Playlist, Pinned Story, Scroll Film, Scroll Glow, Scroll Showcase, Slideshow, Split Text, Video Carousel.
  • Marketing: Call to Action, Count Up, Countdown, Counter Cards, Mortgage Calculator, Price List, Price Table, Property Card, Reviews, Skills Measurement, Social Share, Team Members, Testimonial Carousel.
  • Posts and site: Archive Posts, Author Info Card, Featured Image, Page Title, Portfolio, Post Comments, Post Excerpt, Post Info, Post Navigation, Posts, Site Logo, Site Title, Sitemap, Yoast Breadcrumbs.
  • Navigation and tools: Google Maps, Nav Menu, Scroll to Top, Search, Single Page Navigation.

Sentio Premium

Sentio Premium is a separate plugin from sentioaddons.com. It adds credits every month, films made for your pages by Sentio Studio, advanced motion (pins, scrubs, smooth scrolling) and 171 widgets in all, with sets for WooCommerce, The Events Calendar and ACF. Premium’s extra widgets show in the Elementor panel as locked entries. They are names only: no Premium code ships in this plugin.

External services

Sentio AI is off until an administrator switches it on, and nothing below that belongs to it is contacted before then. The other services are contacted only by a widget you place, or after you opt in. Nothing about your visitors is ever sent to Sentio.

sentioaddons.com: your Sentio AI account and credits

Needed to switch Sentio AI on and to count credits. Requests are made by your server.

  • When you switch it on: your site’s address, this plugin’s name and version, the email address you enter, and whether you ticked the updates box go to https://sentioaddons.com/wp-json/sentio-lm/v1/ai/register. Sentio emails that address a 6-digit code; the code you type is checked at /ai/verify-code.
  • When you open the Sentio AI panel or the Sentio dashboard: your site’s address and its registration token, to read your credit balance (/ai/status, /ai/credits/balance).
  • Before and after each build or change: the same, with what kind of thing is being made (a page, a picture, a change), and afterwards whether it worked and how much AI it used (/ai/authorize, /ai/report, /ai/credits/quote, /ai/credits/free, /ai/credits/result). Your words and your page’s content are never sent here.
  • To give free credits once per site, the service calls your site back once at /wp-json/sentio/v1/ai/credit-challenge. Your site answers with a proof that it holds the registration, and nothing else.

Sentio uses Klaviyo (Klaviyo, Inc.) to store the email address behind a free account, and to send you Sentio updates only if you ticked that box. This plugin never talks to Klaviyo itself.

  • Terms: https://sentioaddons.com/credit-terms/
  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai
  • Klaviyo privacy: https://www.klaviyo.com/legal/privacy/privacy-notice

Sentio’s AI service: building and changing pages

Needed to plan and write a page. It is run by Sentio (Sensus Media) on Google Cloud, at addresses the account service hands out (today https://generate-gsbgom2zpa-uc.a.run.app and https://engine-gsbgom2zpa-uc.a.run.app). It passes what a build needs to Anthropic, whose models do the writing. Some requests are made by your server and others by your browser while you work in the Elementor editor.

Sent when you build a page or ask for a change:

  • the words you type and your answers to Sentio’s questions;
  • what you attach: a mockup or PDF is sent whole; photos and a logo as small copies; stills from a film, never the film itself;
  • a web address you give it. The service opens that page to read its layout and motion;
  • the settings and text of the part of the page you are changing, and pictures of the page in the editor, so the result can be checked;
  • your Elementor global colours and fonts; your site’s title, tagline and language; your site brief, when you let Sentio use it; the title, alt text and address of recent images in your Media Library; and on a product page, that WooCommerce product’s public details.

Not sent: anything about your visitors, your other pages, or your site’s users and passwords.

  • Terms: https://sentioaddons.com/credit-terms/
  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai
  • Anthropic terms: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/commercial-terms
  • Anthropic privacy: https://www.anthropic.com/legal/privacy

fal.ai: Sentio Studio pictures

Used only when you say yes to “Add pictures from Sentio Studio?”. Your browser sends Sentio’s AI service a short description written by your site (the page’s subject, colours and look) and, where there is one, the picture to start from. The service passes them to fal.ai, which makes the picture. Your server then downloads the finished file from fal.ai’s file host (*.fal.media) into your Media Library.

  • fal.ai terms: https://fal.ai/terms
  • fal.ai privacy: https://fal.ai/privacy

Pixabay: stock photos

When a page built from your words has places for photos and you have none, Sentio’s AI service searches Pixabay with a few words about the page. Your server then downloads the photos it uses from https://pixabay.com/ into your Media Library, each credited to its photographer. Pixabay receives the search words from Sentio, and an ordinary download request from your server.

  • Pixabay terms: https://pixabay.com/service/terms/
  • Pixabay privacy: https://pixabay.com/service/privacy/

sentioaddons.com: ready-made pages, their films and preview clips

Only after Sentio AI is switched on. When you pick a ready-made page, your server downloads that page, its pictures and its film from https://sentioaddons.com/wp-content/uploads/sentio-demo/ and checks every file before keeping it. The cards on Sentio → AI and the dashboard also play short preview clips from the same folder, loaded by your browser. These are ordinary downloads: they carry your site’s address, as every request from WordPress does, and nothing else.

  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/#sentio-ai

A site you point Sentio at

When you ask Sentio to build from a web address, Sentio’s AI service visits that address. A page built this way uses that site’s own pictures and films as stand-ins, linked from where they are, until you replace them with yours: while they are on your page, your visitors’ browsers load them from that site. On Sentio → AI → Direction, “match a site” makes your server read the address you type, and its stylesheets, to pick up its colours and fonts.

Google Fonts

A page Sentio builds or places uses the fonts its design calls for. When those are Google fonts, your visitors’ browsers load them from https://fonts.googleapis.com and https://fonts.gstatic.com, as they do for any Elementor page that uses Google fonts. The Elementor editor loads them the same way while you work.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/fonts/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Google Maps

Widget: Google Maps. Your visitor’s browser loads https://maps.googleapis.com/maps/api/js only when a Google Maps widget is on the page and you have set a Google API key. With no key the widget contacts nobody. Data sent: your API key and the standard Maps JavaScript API load parameters.

  • Terms: https://developers.google.com/maps/terms-20180207
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

YouTube

Widgets: Media Playlist, Video Carousel, Portfolio, only when you give one a YouTube address. Your visitor’s browser loads the thumbnail from https://img.youtube.com/, the player from https://www.youtube.com/embed/ and the playback API from https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api. Data sent: the public video ID.

  • Terms: https://www.youtube.com/t/terms
  • Privacy: https://policies.google.com/privacy

Vimeo

Widgets: Media Playlist, Video Carousel, Portfolio, only when you give one a Vimeo address. Your visitor’s browser loads the player from https://player.vimeo.com/. When no thumbnail is set by hand, your server also asks https://vimeo.com/api/oembed.json for one. Data sent: the public video ID or address.

  • Terms: https://vimeo.com/terms
  • Privacy: https://vimeo.com/privacy

cdnjs (Cloudflare): the Lottie player

Widget: Lottie. A page with a Lottie widget loads the lottie-web player, version 5.12.2, from https://cdnjs.cloudflare.com/, and the animation file from the address you give the widget. Data sent: nothing beyond the request itself.

  • Terms: https://www.cloudflare.com/website-terms/
  • Privacy: https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/

sentioaddons.com: usage data (opt-in)

Off unless you tick the unticked usage-data box on the welcome screen, or opt in at Sentio → Version. Then your server posts once a day to https://sentioaddons.com/wp-json/sentio-lm/v1/telemetry: this plugin’s name and version, your WordPress and PHP versions, your theme’s family, your site’s language, a one-way hash of your site’s address, and how many of each Sentio widget your pages use. Opting out at Sentio → Version asks the service to delete your site’s row (/telemetry/site) and stops the daily post.

  • Privacy: https://sentioaddons.com/privacy-policy/

sentioaddons.com: backlink (per widget, off by default)

Makes no request. A switch on each widget’s Advanced tab, off by default, adds a plain link to that widget’s page on sentioaddons.com. Listed here so nothing is left out.
